                                      PROJECT NO. 59142


 REVIEW OF ERCOT’S                                 §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES                         §
 FOR LARGE LOADS                                   §                     OF TEXAS

             IONIC DIGITAL INC.’S COMMENTS REGARDING ERCOT’S
             REQUESTS FOR GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTIONS RELATING TO
                           BATCH ZERO DEADLINES

                                      I.     INTRODUCTION

       Ionic Digital Inc. (“Ionic Digital”) submits these comments regarding Electric Reliability

Council of Texas, Inc.’s (“ERCOT”) August 10, 2026 requests for Good Cause Exceptions relating

to Batch Zero deadlines (“Good Cause Exceptions”). Ionic Digital supports Governor Abbott’s

directed verification of Batch Zero projects and collection of community impact information and

will cooperate with reasonable requests to complete those efforts.

       ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.1(8) already authorizes ERCOT to request materials

supporting Batch Zero eligibility attestations and verify site readiness. Ionic Digital supports use

of that authority and the targeted procedural relief needed to complete verification.

       In granting that relief, Ionic Digital respectfully requests that the Commission confirm:

                  Verification should apply the substantive eligibility criteria and applicable dates

                   established in existing rules, without creating new substantive requirements;


                  Community impact information should be collected and considered consistently

                   with the existing Batch Zero eligibility framework; and




                                                 1
                        Consistent with the Governor’s directive and operational feasibility, ERCOT

                        should retain flexibility to issue Batch Zero classifications on a rolling basis

                        once project-specific verification is complete.


1.         ERCOT’s verification should apply existing eligibility criteria and procedural
           protections.

           PGRR145 expressly provides for verification of Batch Zero eligibility attestations. ERCOT

Planning Guide § 9.1(8) authorizes ERCOT, from July 10, 2026 through April 9, 2027, to request

supporting materials and verify site readiness. If ERCOT identifies an inconsistency, it must

provide notice through the interconnecting Transmission and/or Distribution Service Provider

(“TDSP”) and a reasonable opportunity to explain before determining that an attestation is false in

any material respect and removing the Large Load from Batch Zero.1

           ERCOT should determine whether an Interconnecting Large Load Entity (“ILLE”)

satisfied the applicable eligibility criteria and dates under the requirements then in effect, without

retroactively imposing later-created substantive requirements. Later procedural changes should not

reset or diminish the treatment of prior or existing studies, agreements, Initial Energization

approvals, Load Commissioning Plans (“LCPs”), transmission improvements, planning

milestones, or other milestones recognized under existing rules.


2.         Procedural changes to Batch Zero should preserve the treatment of established
           project milestones.

           ERCOT Planning Guide § 9 gives specified milestones significance under the applicable

eligibility pathway, including Initial Energization, qualifying studies, executed agreements, LCPs,

and transmission planning milestones. Changes to Batch Zero timing or administration should



1
    See ERCOT Planning Guide, § 9.1(8), Large Load Interconnection or Modification (Jul. 11, 2026).


                                                         2
 preserve those milestones and should not require projects to reestablish matters already addressed

through applicable studies, agreements, approvals, or planning processes.


3.     Community impact information should be incorporated consistently with the Batch
       Zero framework.

       Ionic Digital supports collection of the information identified in the Governor’s August 3,

2026 directive. That information will assist the Commission and the Legislature in evaluating

broader policy considerations concerning data center development in Texas.

       ERCOT’s August 10 filing recognizes that eligibility verification and community impact

information serve related but distinct purposes. Eligibility verification confirms whether an ILLE

satisfied the requirements supporting Batch Zero classification, while community impact

information provides a broader record concerning data center development. Ionic Digital requests

clear guidance so that Batch Zero eligibility determinations remain administered under Planning

Guide § 9 while the additional information informs the State’s broader policy review.


4.     ERCOT should retain flexibility to classify verified projects on a rolling basis where
       consistent with the Governor’s directive and operationally feasible.

       Ionic Digital respectfully requests that the Commission authorize ERCOT, consistent with

the Governor’s directive and where operationally feasible, to issue Batch Zero classifications on a

rolling basis once verification of an individual project is complete, without waiting for review of

the full Batch Zero population. ERCOT has indicated that the verification and audit process will

take several months.

       Once ERCOT determines that a project satisfies the applicable eligibility criteria,

withholding classification until the broader review is complete could create avoidable delays

affecting financing, contractual commitments, construction sequencing, and planned energization.



                                                3
 Rolling classification would provide greater certainty without authorizing energization or relieving

any project of applicable QSA, interconnection, modeling, or operational requirements. If rolling

classification is not operationally feasible, Ionic Digital requests reasonable visibility into the

classification schedule and sequencing considerations affecting verified projects.

                                       II.     CONCLUSION

       For these reasons, Ionic Digital supports the targeted procedural relief requested in

ERCOT’s August 10 filing, subject to the principles described above.

       Ionic Digital further requests that the Commission confirm that the Good Cause Exceptions

are procedural and do not, by themselves, alter the treatment under existing ERCOT rules of prior

studies, executed agreements, Initial Energization, LCPs, transmission planning milestones, or

other established project commitments. The relief should not prejudice continued recognition of

those milestones or foreclose project-specific treatment, continued processing, or other relief

available under existing ERCOT or Commission authority.



Dated: August 19, 2026

                                                     Respectfully submitted,

                                                     /s/ Richard Carson
                                                     Richard Carson
                                                     General Counsel
                                                     Ionic Digital Inc.
                                                     richard.carson@ionicdigital.com
                                                     918.574.4571

                                      PROJECT NO. 59142

                           COMMENTS OF IONIC DIGITAL INC.

                                  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

   Support for verification and targeted procedural relief. Ionic Digital supports the
    Governor’s verification directive regarding Batch Zero projects, ERCOT’s collection of
    community impact information, and the targeted Good Cause Exceptions necessary to
    complete those efforts.

   Apply existing Batch Zero eligibility standards. ERCOT’s verification should determine
    whether projects satisfied the eligibility criteria and applicable deadlines established under
    ERCOT Planning Guide § 9 and PGRR145. The process should not create or retroactively
    impose new substantive eligibility requirements. Planning Guide § 9.1(8) authorizes ERCOT
    to request supporting information and provides ILLEs an opportunity to address identified
    inconsistencies before removal from Batch Zero.

   Preserve established project milestones and reliance interests. Procedural changes to Batch
    Zero should not alter the treatment afforded to milestones already recognized under applicable
    ERCOT rules and processes, including Initial Energization, qualifying studies, executed
    agreements, LCPs, transmission improvements, and transmission planning milestones.
    Projects should not be required to reestablish matters previously addressed through applicable
    studies, agreements, approvals, or planning processes.

   Maintain the distinction between Batch Zero eligibility verification and community
    impact review. Community impact information may appropriately inform broader policy
    decisions by the Governor, Commission, and Legislature, but its collection and consideration
    should be administered consistently with the existing Batch Zero framework. The Commission
    should provide clear guidance regarding how that information will be used so that Batch Zero
    eligibility continues to be determined under ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.

   Permit rolling classification of verified projects. Where consistent with the Governor’s
    directive and operationally feasible, ERCOT should be authorized to issue Batch Zero
    classifications on a rolling basis once project specific verification is complete. Requiring a
    verified project to await completion of the full Batch Zero review could unnecessarily affect
    financing, contractual commitments, construction sequencing, and planned energization.
    Classification itself would not authorize energization or excuse compliance with applicable
    QSA, modeling, interconnection, or operational requirements.

   Confirm that the requested relief is procedural only. The Commission should clarify that
    the Good Cause Exceptions do not alter the substantive treatment of prior studies, agreements,
    approvals, or established project commitments, and do not foreclose project specific treatment
    or other relief available under existing ERCOT or Commission authority. If rolling
    classification is not feasible, ERCOT should provide reasonable visibility into the anticipated
    classification schedule and sequencing.
